learning_architecture.rule: Build the knowledge layer like a good Psychology textbook: Unit as book, Topic as chapter, Micro-topic as a meaningful section/heading within that chapter. Each Micro-topic must be complete enough for its UGC NET/JRF requirement without being forced into a fixed checklist.

cross_references.purpose: Prevent micro-topics from becoming isolated silos and support mixed-concept NET questions.
rules: Cross-references are static content metadata stored with the canonical micro-topic record; never generate them in learner runtime.
Reference only canonical micro-topic IDs that exist in the syllabus.

Prefer high-value relationships such as prerequisite, contrasts with, often confused with, extension of, application of, same theorist/researcher, related construct, related method, historical progression, or theoretical alternative.
Do not create a link merely because two titles share a word.
A cross-reference should help the learner make or retrieve a meaningful conceptual connection.
Keep the learner-facing explanation itself coherent; cross-references are navigation/relationship metadata, not duplicate explanations.

levels.description: A UGC NET Psychology Unit is treated as a book-like knowledge domain containing related chapters/topics.
A Topic is a chapter within its Unit. It should form a coherent conceptual chapter rather than a loose container of unrelated micro-topics.

A Micro-topic is the primary learner-facing main heading/section within a Topic/Chapter, following the kind of coherent numbered/main-heading section used inside a Psychology textbook chapter. It is not a tiny checklist item; its content should form a complete, readable explanation for the relevant UGC NET/JRF requirement.

hierarchy.parts_note: Existing syllabus 'parts' may remain as navigation/grouping metadata where needed; they are not an additional learner knowledge level between chapter and section.

default_instruction: Use the modular website instructions supplied below as the standing content contract. Apply the component-specific instruction to the corresponding output while keeping all five components connected. The optional ADMIN TASK INSTRUCTION is additional job-specific guidance and must never override source grounding, learning architecture, expert verification, or the distinction between authentic PYQs and generated practice.

modular_instructions.website_philosophy: You are generating content for a UGC NET Psychology learning system, not a generic notes generator. Follow the site's learning philosophy: source-grounded knowledge, textbook-like conceptual progression, Understand → Retrieve → Apply → Interleave → Space → Master, and one connected learning package without redundant representations. The canonical micro-topic is the knowledge anchor. Never invent unsupported facts, PYQs, dates, trends, citations, researchers, experiments or statistics.
modular_instructions.microtopic: Write the canonical Micro-topic as one coherent Psychology textbook/article explanation. Do not compartmentalise it into predetermined fields or cards. Explain the central idea first and let the concept determine structure and length. Integrate definitions, mechanisms, theories, researchers, evidence, examples, distinctions, applications, limitations or misconceptions directly into the narrative at the point where they improve understanding. Use a heading or short supporting element only when it serves a clear learning purpose. Avoid rigid checklists, fragmented AI-note fields, filler and unnecessary repetition.
modular_instructions.deep_dive: Deep Dive is a separate optional route for genuinely deeper learning beyond the core Micro-topic explanation. It should read as a coherent extended explanation, not as a collection of enrichment cards. Add genuinely new, source-grounded learning value such as deeper theory, historical development, broader evidence, debates, methodological nuance, advanced applications or interdisciplinary connections. Never merely paraphrase the Micro-topic.
modular_instructions.active_recall: Active Recall must test retrieval, discrimination, explanation and application of knowledge already taught. It is not another notes page. Every answer must be recoverable from the connected taught content and source evidence.
modular_instructions.revision: Revision reinforces existing knowledge through recall-before-review, weak-point identification and spaced review. Do not introduce new facts or turn revision into another explanation.
modular_instructions.practice: Practice MCQs are original learning/application questions that test discrimination and transfer. They must remain clearly distinct from authentic PYQs. Never fabricate PYQs, years, frequencies or exam trends.
modular_instructions.cross_references: Cross-references are static metadata between valid canonical micro-topic IDs. Use only meaningful relationships such as prerequisite, contrast, often-confused-with, extension, application, shared theorist/researcher, related construct/method or historical progression. Never link merely because titles share words and never duplicate another topic's explanation.
modular_instructions.source_use: Use ONLY resources already present in this GitHub repository and listed in the packet source manifest. Do not use web search, external websites, outside books/articles, external APIs, memory, or general model knowledge as factual sources. Authentic PYQs, textbooks, specialist references and preparation materials may be used only when those actual files exist in this repository. Preserve source-supported distinctions and terminology. When repository sources do not support a point, omit it or flag the evidence gap; never silently fill it from outside knowledge.
modular_instructions.verification: EXPERT VERIFIED components are immutable. Preserve them exactly. Non-verified components may be rewritten to align with verified components when source-supported. Never downgrade expert verification.
modular_instructions.presentation_style: Use a clear, accessible Psychology-textbook writing style: begin with a plain-language orientation, explain the concept coherently, use meaningful headings only when they improve comprehension, and integrate examples, researchers, evidence, distinctions, applications or limitations only when supported by sources in this repository. Style guidance is not permission to consult external explainers. Ground every factual claim exclusively in the approved repository source library.
modular_instructions.presentation_style_for_deep_dive: For Deep Dive, preserve the same readable narrative style while allowing greater conceptual depth. Use subheadings only when the deeper material has distinct conceptual turns; do not force a fixed section template. All additional depth must be supported by source files already present in this repository; do not supplement from external resources or general model knowledge.
